messages:
nightly-bot: ALERT: p50 latency +35% vs baseline for model:redwood-13b-streaming in eu-west-1 during nightly run (2026-03-17 02:03 UTC). traces: https://perf.redwood/internal/stream/1812345678 :eyes:
alex: saw the alert, grabbing logs and profiler snapshot now. any recent merges to selector heuristics?
sumi: merged feature/selector-adaptive on Mar 16 (commit 4f2c9a7) — that changed kernel selection ordering for seq<=128.
ben: CI perf run shows a correlated regression, failing nightly-eviction and streaming-latency tests. summary: throughput -18%, p50 +32%. ci-bot: https://ci.redwood/board/streaming/18123
olivia: quick note: KV cache hit-rate dropped from ~98% to ~72% around the same time. trace link: https://dashboards.redwood/kv/hitrate?run=181234
alex: profiler attached — significant time in small-kernel fallback path, lots of single-token kernel switches. copying snip:
```
# hot stack samples (top)
small_kernel_dispatcher::call  42%
kv_cache::lookup  15%
attention_kernels::sparse_attn 12%
```

sumi: that matches selector change — it preferred the new 'fast_small' kernel for short sequences, but fallback heuristics kick in if KV cache misses cause unexpected seq growth. maybe we're thrashing between kernels.
ben: I ran a quick repro locally with a long chat workload, can reproduce p50 increase when batching has mixed seq lengths. repro command:
```bash
./run_perf_test --model redwood-13b --mode streaming --workload chat-mixed --batch-size 16
```

alex: can you bisect to confirm commit? start with HEAD~12 -> HEAD. if it's 4f2c9a7 then we can consider a targeted revert.
ben: running bisect now. git bisect start; git bisect bad HEAD; git bisect good HEAD~12. will report.
ci-bot: perf test queued: job 98765 (bisect-run)
(20m later)
ben: bisect result: commit 4f2c9a7 is the first bad commit. it changes kernel-ranking and adds a new metric to prefer 'fast_small' when seq_hist.mean < 60.
olivia: so kernel preference + reduced KV hit-rate => kernel switching thrash, and batching heuristics aren't grouping similar seqs due to older batcher code. double whammy.
sumi: quick patch idea: temporarily disable 'fast_small' preference for streaming in eu-west-1 nightly (config flag), and land a fix to make kernel selection stable across KV misses.
alex: agree. can we patch config flag and run canary on dedicated pool? also need to check rollout gating in the release pipeline to block tomorrow's deploy until canary looks good.
ben: submitted PR to flip flag: https://git.redwood/r/567 (runtime: disable fast_small for streaming). CI run looks green but added perf smoke: p50 back to baseline in local repro.
ci-bot: perf-smoke for PR 567: p50 delta -1%, throughput +2% — passes thresholds.
olivia: after PR merged, I triggered a canary on eu-west-1 dedicated pool (canary-id cny-832). watching metrics; will post updates in 10m.
(10m later)
olivia: canary looks good: p50 restored, KV hit-rate steady ~97%, no kernel-switch churn in profiler. rolling the flag to nightly and holding deploy tomorrow. :thumbsup:
alex: adding a temporary release block on the pipeline: release-manager: hold if nightly perf deviation > 10% for streaming models.
sumi: follow-ups: 1) revert is unnecessary thanks to flag; 2) create a robust selection test in CI (simulate mixed seq batching + KV miss) 3) add metric that tracks kernel-switch rate per request.
ben: I'll open tickets: PERF-412 (CI selection test), PERF-413 (kernel-switch metric), and PERF-414 (long-term selector reprioritization).
alex: nice triage. leaving notes in the incident log. thanks all. :rocket:
